answer: One identity tends one lotus in a pond and locks a 110-credit bond. The lotus grows 12 to 20 centimetres per epoch to a zenith for 30 credits, and a sparrow auditor measures it and records growth; a mismatch burns the bond. The kth lotus costs 140 credits, so 1,000 lotuses cost 140,000 credits and need 1,000 ponds, because crowded lotuses in one pond grow below 12 centimetres and lose their bonds. A rented-growth ring fails: the sparrow auditor remeasures each lotus, and each zenith record binds to a pond and an epoch. An honest grower tends one lotus, pays 140 credits, and recovers the bond.
